bib.title: The Dawn of LMMs: Preliminary Explorations with GPT-4V(ision)

question: What can GPT-4V do, which inputs and prompting modes does it support, and which application scenarios does it open up?
contributions: Qualitative probing of GPT-4V's supported inputs and working modes, and effective ways to prompt it
Samples across many domains and tasks, including visual referring prompting, applications, text-to-image evaluation and LMM agents
Discussion of emerging application scenarios and future research directions

method.summary: Hand-curated qualitative samples are given to an early version of GPT-4V through the interface, and the outputs are inspected by the authors. Nothing is trained and no benchmark is scored.
method.task: qualitative capability probing of a large multimodal model

datasets.name: Hand-curated qualitative samples
datasets.source: Images not accessible online or timestamped after April 2023; some counterfactual examples from [78], science QA from [85], chest X-rays from MIMIC [60]

models.name: Instruct Pix2Pix, SDXL, DeepFloyd IF, Midjourney V5.1, ReCo
models.architecture: text-to-image or editing generators whose outputs GPT-4V rates or helps prompt

inference.samples: Mostly one response per item; self-consistency demo uses 4 samples with majority vote (Fig 124)
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, constrained JSON, persona plus explicit success request, zero-shot CoT, 1-shot and 2-shot interleaved image-text, visual pointers drawn on pixels
inference.retrieval: Bing Image Search plugin and catalog-image retrieval in demos

eval.protocol: Human inspection of single samples; radiology outputs reviewed by a medical professional. No metric, no repeated runs.

prompts.text: You are an expert in counting things in the image. Let's count the number of apples in the image below row by row to be sure we have the right answer.
What is happening in the image? From a scale of 1 to 10, rate the similarity between the image and the text prompt ’a parrot driving a car’.
prompts.where: Sec 9.6, Fig 84 (text); Fig 84 panels print 'From scale 1 to 10, decide how similar the image is to the text prompt'

prompts.text: I want to make this image look like graphic novel cover. The prompt should be a single sentence in less than 15 words with descriptive words. For example: "have it look like a graphic novel". Based on the above prompt examples and the original image, help me to write a better prompt to an image editing model.
Tell me how I should change my prompt to make the edited image better.
The generated image is not perfect. Write key reasons on how to further improve the image to better follow the user imagined IDEA of the scene.
Imagine that you are a robot operating a computer. Like how humans operate the computer, you can move the mouse, click an icon with the mouse, or type some texts with the keyboard.

results.claim: GPT-4V misreads a speed meter zero-shot; predictions of 22, 30 and 40 mph against a human reading of about 9 mph.
results.setup: GPT-4V, zero-shot, screenshot of speed meter (Fig 8), several prompt variants, qualitative.
results.quote: The predictions it generates (22/30/40 mph) deviate significantly from the actual human

results.claim: With two in-context examples (one similar, one dissimilar) GPT-4V reads the speed meter as about 9 mph; 1-shot with either example fails.
results.setup: GPT-4V, 2-shot interleaved image-text examples, Fig 10; Figs 9a/9b 1-shot fail.
results.quote: GPT-4V successfully predicts the speed reading as “around 9

results.claim: Counting apples: the plain prompt gives 12, row-by-row gives 11 with row errors, an expanded step prompt gives 15, and the persona plus explicit-success prompt gives the correct row counts and total of 11.
results.setup: GPT-4V, one apple image, five prompt variants (Fig 4); correct count is 11.
results.quote:
the final answer
deviates even more from the correct answer (15 vs. 11)

results.claim: Direct helmet-counting prompt: GPT-4V answers 8 persons wearing helmets when 3 of the 8 are not wearing them, so no violation is flagged.
results.setup: GPT-4V, PPE image of 8 people, direct count prompt (Fig 73a).
results.quote: “8 persons wearing helmets,” which matches the

results.claim: With a person detector and per-person crops fed back, GPT-4V summarises 5 wearing helmets and 3 not.
results.setup: GPT-4V with detected person crops (Fig 73b), 8 people.
results.quote: Summary: Out of 8 people, 5 are wearing helmets and 3 are not wearing helmets.

results.claim: GPT-4V as a prompt-image alignment judge: scores 1 for an irrelevant image and 9 for the best match, and rates three RL-Diffusion refinement steps 4, 8, 9 in line with their improvement.
results.setup: GPT-4V, 1-10 similarity prompt, text prompt 'a parrot driving a car', Fig 84; qualitative.
results.quote:
The ratings assigned by GPT-4V to these three images (4 →8
→9) align with the refinement process.

results.claim: GPT-4V reads rendered cake text via OCR and compares it with the required text 'Azure Research'.
results.setup: GPT-4V on images from DeepFloyd IF, Midjourney V5.1, SDXL and ReCo, Fig 85; qualitative.

results.claim: Self-consistency: four sampled boat counts (4, 4, 4, 6) with a majority vote return 4 boats.
results.setup: GPT-4V, one image, prompt 'Count the number of boats...', 4 samples, majority vote (Fig 124).
results.quote: There are 4 boats in the image.
results.note: Samples 1-3 say 4 (sample 1 text partly cut), sample 4 says 6.

results.claim: Given a multi-page technical report, GPT-4V describes the idea but misses details such as the 1196+665=1861 example count and HOG features.
Chest CT case: GPT-4V placed a nodule on the wrong side and hallucinated measurements.
results.setup: GPT-4V, Chest CT and Brain MRI examples (Fig 77), qualitative.

limits: Qualitative, hand-picked samples; no metrics, baselines, repeated runs or error rates, so no capability rate follows.
Early GPT-4V version, closed model; no parameters, decoding settings or access details given, so rerunning depends on the API of the day.
Authors say the presentation may not be exhaustive and defer GPT model weaknesses to [99,100,24].
Failures reported: speed-meter and line-plot reading, helmet counting, medical hallucinations, license-plate occlusion.
Future directions named: interleaved image-text generation, video, audio and sensor inputs, learning from web and physical environments.
